A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original HCNet results for inductive and transductive link prediction, component ablations, knowledge-graph experiments, and an arity-based analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original HCNet experiments and additionally reports HyperCycle classification results and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed initialization, query conditioning, positional encoding, message passing, decoder, and training loss are retained. v2's explicit affine update spells out the linear map followed by nonlinearity already specified in v1; the newly evaluated HRNet serves as a control.

E1.justification: v2 adds one focused synthetic scenario: HyperCycle graphs with alternating relations and hyperedge arities 3–7, testing classification of opposite-node versus two-hop links. All earlier real-world hypergraph and knowledge-graph datasets remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds G-MPNN to the transductive JF17K comparison, reporting MRR 0.501; it was absent from v1 Table 2. Appendix N also experimentally compares HCNet against HRNet, which v1 discussed only for complexity analysis. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: JF17K's reported training count changes from 77,733 with no listed validation count to 61,104 training and 15,275 validation examples; its GNN hidden dimension changes from 32 to 64. Tables 12–13 also revise batching and accumulation for WP-IND, JF-IND, and FB-AUTO while retaining effective batch size 32. HyperCycle introduces a 70/30 graph split and accuracy evaluation. These establish substantive reported setting revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix N adds a controlled expressiveness analysis comparing HCNet and HRNet with matching message-passing components on symmetric cyclic graphs. It tests whether query conditioning overcomes unary-encoder indistinguishability. The existing initialization, positional-encoding, and arity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports five-seed averages without uncertainty estimates. v2 adds HCNet standard deviations across all five main relational-hypergraph benchmarks in Tables 5 and 14, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. Both versions specify five runs; no increase in repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Reported JF17K HCNet MRR changes from 0.525 to 0.540 and Hits@10 from 0.718 to 0.730, with updated arity-specific results. These accompany revised settings and are not same-setting gains. v2 also adds HyperCycle accuracy of 100% for HCNet versus 50% for HRNet and resource measurements. Inductive, FB-AUTO, knowledge-graph, and component-ablation means remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit R-MPNN containment theorem and proof in Appendix C, constructions relating existing architectures to HR-MPNNs, and counterexample reasoning about indistinguishable nodes. The central WL, logical-expressiveness, and k-ary-invariant results are retained; notably, v2 Theorem 5.3 already appeared as v1 Theorem E.1.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: conditional message passing for relational hypergraphs, stronger expressiveness than unary relational encoders, strong inductive performance, and state-of-the-art transductive results. The revised introduction and added experiments reorganize and support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The new HyperCycle discussion explains the performance separation through source-conditioned distance information. Section 7 additionally states that the approach is limited to link prediction and identifies complex query answering as future work. The earlier scalability limitation and most existing result interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents HyperCycle generation, its training configuration, and the HRNet control. Table 19 adds A10 training/testing times and GPU memory usage, specifying testing batch size 1. The anonymous code pointer changes from the HC-MPNN project to HCNet; extensive earlier implementation and loss details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix B substantially expand positioning by distinguishing ordered relational hypergraphs from qualifier-based hyper-relational knowledge graphs and role-value n-ary representations, arguing that the paper's setting is more general. Relevant additions include Galkin et al. on hyper-relational message passing and Xiong et al. on shrinking embeddings; the earlier ULTRA discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, with explicit motivation, approach, and expressiveness questions. Knowledge-graph theory and transductive experiments move to appendices, theoretical subsections and appendices are reorganized, and worked logical examples expand the explanations.

P2.justification: v2 redraws retained illustrations, removes v1's separate computational-graph figure, and adds indistinguishability, representation-comparison, and HyperCycle diagrams. It places ablation tables side by side, relocates the transductive table, transposes dataset statistics, adds uncertainty and resource displays, and changes the document's overall layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency and support through standard deviations for primary results, a matched synthetic expressiveness comparison, resource measurements, and a more explicit containment argument. Clearer positioning and organization also help explain the contribution. These are useful supporting gains: the core method and most benchmark findings remain stable, and higher JF17K scores cannot establish a direct improvement because its reported split and model width changed.
